title: Hello, what would be the best version for beginners?

posts.author: PixelDarkKnight0193
posts.body:
Soy nuevo aquí y me gustaria saber cual es la mejor versión de RPG Maker para principiantes, ahora iba a probar con el RPG Maker VX Ace, ya que tengo un portátil humilde y seguramente el rendimiento de mi procesador no es muy bueno. Ire pidiendo consejo mientras toqueteo cosas
I am new here and I would like to know which is the best version of RPG Maker for beginners, now I was going to try with the RPG Maker VX Ace, since I have a humble laptop and surely the performance of my processor is not very good. I'll be asking for advice while I touch things

posts.author: SoulCatapult
posts.body: MV. For me, games made in MV run even better than those in VX Ace. Plus the default resolution is much larger, and the plugins are a lot more user-friendly than Ruby Scripts. Being able to use a side-view battle system out of the box is also very nice.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
MV or MZ. You'll find the most support for those. If you have trouble you'll get answers for those the fastest.
MV: Cheaper, more plugins, Yanfly plugins (MV) are cheaper than VisuStella (MZ) and Yanfly code is open so compatability issues can be fixed and you can tweak and edit them as you like.
MZ: More QoL features in the editor itself, particularly the map editor, but there's a
new tool
that lets MV users get the same map editor

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
Welcome to the forums!
This has been asked many times. I suggest doing research on the differences among the versions to see which one might be best for you and your specific interests.
Often the advice will be if you are just starting out, to pick MZ. But it can be fairly nuanced.
You can find lots of posts and videos comparing the different RPG Makers and offering advice.
All I can say is that about 3 years ago, I did that research and I decided to go with MZ. And I don't regret it.

posts.author: kirbwarrior
posts.body: Importantly, your operating system really matters. If you have Windows, all makers work for you. But I think only MV has native Linux support and I think only MV and MZ have Mac support.

posts.author: Piyan Glupak
posts.body:
I use MV because my laptop doesn't have the capability to run MZ (for instance, it has only 2 Mb of RAM). When I get a new computer I will try MZ. (RPG Maker does free trials for up to a month.) It sounds to me as if the OP might be in a similar position to me.
Both VX Ace and MV are good, and easy for a beginner to use. The reason that I switched to MV when it was fairly new was that I preferred the bigger tiles and sprites. Other reasons that I was glad that I switched include the character generator of MV gives better results than the VX Ace one and that I can use MV with Linux, and you can do a little more placing tiles when mapping with MV. There are a few minor changes to the editor, for instance, MV lets you have up to 6 options on choices. However, I prefer the tile sets and sprites of MV.
If I was in OP's position, I use free trials for a month option to decide what I wanted.

posts.author: ISC
posts.body:
The version I’d recommend to anyone starting now is definitely MZ. Aside from the advantages already mentioned, I’d add that MZ is regularly updated, so over time, it could see some strong development. Personally, I also like how MZ handles plugin commands compared to MV—these small improvements might become more appreciated over time compared to previous versions. Of course, excluding plugins and custom scripts, every version has its own charm, but looking ahead, MZ would be my recommendation.
The best way to decide, in my opinion, is to try the trial versions of each and see which one you connect with the most.
There are also more modern versions, like Unite and With, though I don’t think they’ve gained much popularity. Then there's Pixel Game Maker MV (though I'm not entirely sure if it’s technically part of the RPG Maker family, so forgive me if I’m wrong on that)

posts.author: JPlaysan
posts.body: I remember starting out with VX back in 2009 which was my very first RM. I tried to make a game with it but I didn't see it to completion unfortunately. Several years later I would then try MV which I really enjoyed so I would perhaps start with that. Then again, there's MZ which may be more of a preference.

posts.author: fizzly
posts.body: In my opinion, each of them is similar enough that it is easy to jump from one to the other, with the newest one (MZ) offering the most possibilities and continuous support for plugins, so I would ultimately choose this one. However, since you are just starting out, taking into the prices, maybe buy an earlier one on sale, e.g. VX Ace and see if it makes sense to play with this at all - if it suits you or not.

posts.author: Prescott
posts.body: Beginner? The cheapest one. Either 2003 or MV on sale. Just like with expensive music equipment, don't buy the expensive stuff if you're just a beginner. You can't be sure if you'll like it or not until trying it out substantially. If you really end up liking it, then you can look into putting more money into it for something like RPG Maker MZ or even alternative engines that are similar.
